newsitem.title: DUBAI: Dubai gold sellers hope for festival fillip.
newsitem.headline: Dubai gold sellers hope for festival fillip.

text.p: Dubai retail gold turnover is expected to get a boost during a month-long shopping festival underway in the Gulf Arab emirate, traders said on Sunday.

Backers of the Dubai Shopping Festival (DSF), which started on March 27, and its parallel "Dubai city of gold" promotion, expect some two million visitors to come to Dubai in April attracted by bargain jewellery, gold coins, ingots and bars.
"People are now waking up to the festival...we're seeing a good response so far," said one owner of a retail shop in Dubai's sprawling gold souk.

Souk-sellers are expecting large number of visitors from the Indian-subcontinent and other Gulf Arab states to buy gold in Dubai where jewellery making costs and taxes are often lower than in other regional markets and close to spot market rates.
Local newspapers on Sunday carried adverts by Dubai's Gold and Jewellery Group offering raffle draws to win 41 kg of gold at more than 250 local jewellers between March 27-April 26.
Dubai's benchmark Ten Tola (TT) bar -- 3.746 ounces of 24 carat gold -- was at 4,835-4,840 UAE dirhams ($1,317-$1,318) on Sunday, down from 4,875 dirhams on March 24.
Spot gold was last quoted on Friday at $349.50-$350.00 an ounce, down from $352.65-353.15 a week earlier.
"With a large number of visitors from India, jewellery (demand) will go higher," a Dubai-based gold wholesaler said.
Demand in the Gulf was also being fanned by demand in Saudi Arabia with the annual haj pilgrimage of some two million Moslems to Islamic holy sites in the kingdom in April.

Re-export demand into India -- the major market for Dubai gold -- was limited ahead of the start of the next Indian financial year and the expected announcement on Monday of a a new Indian export-import policy that would sweep away a host of import restrictions, traders said.
"Businesses are mainly squaring their books," said one exporter to the Indian market.
Bullion imports into Dubai in March had slowed from February's record monthly level of 56.05 tonnes but were still strong ahead of the shopping festival, traders said. ($1=3.67 UAE dirhams)
